bull.b: Initial Ntrust results show clinically meaningful responses in small autoimmune cohorts, providing evidence that Nkarta’s NK-cell approach can affect disease activity. If replicated with longer follow-up and broader enrollment, this could support development value and future expansion beyond oncology.

An off-the-shelf NK-cell format could make treatment more readily available than individualized cell manufacturing, supporting scalable clinical deployment if efficacy and durability are confirmed. The design may also improve operational flexibility across multiple indications and treatment settings.

Moderate debt relative to equity indicates Nkarta is not currently highly dependent on debt financing, reducing the direct burden of leverage on a development-stage balance sheet. This provides some financial flexibility, although ongoing losses still pressure the company’s capital base.

bear.b: The absence of reported revenue means Nkarta’s programs have not yet produced a commercial funding stream, leaving research and clinical development dependent on existing capital or future financing. This makes progress toward approval and commercialization especially important to long-term viability.

Large and worsening operating losses show that spending remains substantial without revenue to offset research and development costs. Persistent losses can consume shareholder capital, narrow strategic flexibility, and increase the amount of successful execution required before the business can become self-sustaining.

Heavy operating and free-cash-flow burn, combined with a substantial decline in equity, indicates that the company’s financial runway is being consumed while products remain pre-commercial. Continued funding needs could constrain development choices and create dilution or financing pressure over the next several quarters.
